title: Self-supplied oracle AND a one-ulp-wrong want: the fixture `define's all 14 M_* macros it claims to test, and M_LOG10E's want is not the annex's number
detail: Lines 16-29 re-`define every M_* constant, then lines 33-46 CHECKR those same defines back — a compiler shipping no constants.vams passes all 14. VerA does ship them (src/frontend/preprocessor.zig:936 constants_vams, prepended at line 137), so the local defines actively hide the implementation's copy. Stacked on top: line 35 wants M_LOG10E = 0.43429448190325176, exactly one ulp BELOW float('0.43429448190325182765') = 0.4342944819032518 (verified by struct-punned bit diff = 1; |true 1/ln10 - published double| = 1.098e-17 vs |true - written want| = 6.649e-17). The written want is the double-arithmetic result of 1.0/log(10.0), not a value derived from the LRM. Lines 10-11 then use that false 'the LRM is one ulp off' claim to justify CHECKR 1e-15 across all 14 — which is 4.5 ulps of slack at M_E and 7.8 ulps at M_LOG10E. I re-parsed all 14 published decimals (annex-d-stddefs.html:330-343) to binary64 and diffed against the written wants: ulpdiff=0 for 13, ulpdiff=1 for M_LOG10E only. The annex decimals are all correctly rounded; there is no LRM typo to work around.
expected: Delete the 14 `define lines and the ANNEX_D_MATHEMATICAL_CONSTANTS `ifdef guard wrapper (the prelude already supplies the macros; verified `include-free reference resolves). Fix line 35's want to 0.4342944819032518. Promote all 14 CHECKR(...,1e-15) to CHECKX — LRM 3.3 pins real to IEEE-754 binary64 and D.2 pins the decimal, so exactly one double conforms; this is precisely check.vh's stated CHECKX case. Rewrite the header comment: the LRM decimal is correct, the fixture's was not. Add //! lrm D.2.

title: driver_flags_low.va can compile to nothing, and both driver fixtures pin ten of twelve masks only through a permutation-invariant OR
detail: driver_flags_low.va lines 5-7 wrap the ENTIRE module in `ifdef DRIVER_ACCESS_VAMS / `else / `define DRIVER_ACCESS_VAMS 1 ... `endif. The day the implementation ships D.3 and defines that guard, the module vanishes, the file still compiles clean, and the fixture silently asserts nothing — caught only by --strict. A fixture must never be able to compile to nothing. Separately, both files `define the twelve masks themselves and then OR their own defines: low asserts OR==31 and only DRIVER_BEHAVIORAL==16; high asserts OR==2016 and only DRIVER_WAND==1024. Swapping DRIVER_GATE (2) with DRIVER_UDP (4), or DRIVER_SDF (32) with DRIVER_NODELETE (64), leaves both ORs unchanged. D.3 (annex-d-stddefs.html:450-461) assigns each mask a specific bit position and that is the entire content of the file. All existing values verified correct against the annex.
expected: Remove the self-erasing `ifdef/`else/`endif wrapper from driver_flags_low.va unconditionally. In both files add one CHECKI per mask, values read off D.3's 32'b literals: UNKNOWN 0, DELAYED 1, GATE 2, UDP 4, ASSIGN 8, BEHAVIORAL 16, SDF 32, NODELETE 64, NOPREEMPT 128, KERNEL 256, WOR 512, WAND 1024. Keep the two OR checks as the disjointness claim (OR == sum iff the bits are disjoint). Add //! lrm D.3. The masks stay locally `define'd for now — see D-26; `include "driver_access.vams" is E0126 today (verified) and a positive fixture cannot be xfail'd.

title: The four non-default selector fixtures test a private replay of the annex `ifdef chain — and the claimed blocker is false, the re-include route works
detail: physical_constants_nist2018/spice/old/nist2010.va each `define a selector and then `include "physical_constants_select.vh", a 60-line hand-copy of D.2's nested chain living in the fixture directory. What is under test is that copy. A compiler shipping no constants.vams passes all four. The uncovered lens asserted these 'cannot be converted until the harness can pass a -D to the preprocessor before the prelude'. THAT IS FALSE and I verified it by execution: `undef CONSTANTS_VAMS / `define PHYSICAL_CONSTANTS_NIST2018 1 / `include "constants.vams" compiles clean and moves `P_Q from 1.602176462e-19 (the prelude's NIST1998 default) to 1.602176634e-19. CONSTANTS_VAMS is a file-set guard, not one of preprocessor.zig's predefined_macros, so `undef bites; "constants.vams" is in builtin_includes (preprocessor.zig:112). All 20 existing wants verified correct against Annex D.2 — the plumbing is the only defect.
expected:
In each of the four, replace `include "physical_constants_select.vh" with:
`undef CONSTANTS_VAMS
`define PHYSICAL_CONSTANTS_NIST2018 1   (resp. _SPICE / _OLD / _NIST2010)
`include "constants.vams"
Keep the extra lower-priority `defines that make each file a precedence test, and keep every existing want. Promote CHECKR(`P_U0, 1.2566370614359173e-6, 1e-15) to CHECKX — 4.0e-7*M_PI is a single exact multiply. Add //! lrm D.2.

title: Delete the hand-copied selector chain once its five consumers read the implementation's constants.vams
detail: physical_constants_select.vh is a verbatim transcription of Annex D.2's nested `ifdef chain. It is the oracle contamination itself: the five physical_constants_*.va fixtures assert that this file is internally consistent with itself. After D-03 and D-05 it has no consumer. COVERAGE.md:84-85 must lose its trailing note about the shared include.
expected: File removed; `grep -r physical_constants_select tests/` returns nothing outside COVERAGE.md history. Do this only after D-03 and D-05 land, otherwise five fixtures break.

title: The default-arm fixture goes out of its way to include the local copy instead of reading the header it is testing
detail: This is the one selector arm that is directly reachable with no plumbing at all: with no PHYSICAL_CONSTANTS_* macro defined, VerA's prepended constants.vams already resolves `P_Q/`P_K/`P_H/`P_EPS0 to CODATA-1998 and `P_U0 to `P_U0_OLD (verified by execution: `P_Q prints 1.602176462e-19 with no directives). Line 8's `include "physical_constants_select.vh" therefore substitutes the fixture's own file for the compiler's. The five wants are all correct against the annex.
expected: Delete line 8. Macros then come from the implementation. Promote line 16's CHECKR(`P_U0, 1.2566370614359173e-6, 1e-15) to CHECKX. Add //! lrm D.2.

title: celsius_constant.va `define's P_CELSIUS0 itself, so it subtracts its own literal
detail: Line 7 is ``define P_CELSIUS0 273.15`. Line 11's `$temperature - `P_CELSIUS0` is the fixture's own number, and the assertion passes on a compiler that provides no constants.vams. Annex D.2 defines P_CELSIUS0 as 273.15 (annex-d-stddefs.html:388) and VerA's prelude supplies it. The numeric claim itself is sound: 350 K temp directive, exact residue 76.85000000000002 against want 76.85 at 1e-12 — verified 2.8e-14 inside tolerance.
expected: Delete line 7. Add //! lrm D.2. Add a direct check of the constant, which is exact and currently unmade anywhere in the suite: `CHECKX("P_CELSIUS0 is zero Celsius in kelvin", `P_CELSIUS0, 273.15);

title: vacuum_constants.va `define's P_C, M_PI and P_U0_OLD itself — and no fixture anywhere proves P_U0_OLD's parentheses survive expansion
detail: Lines 7-9 re-define all three macros under test, so every assertion runs against the fixture's own text rather than the prelude's constants.vams, which contains exactly these three. Second, independent defect: D.2 defines `P_U0_OLD (4.0e-7 * `M_PI)` — the only constant in the file whose body is an expression, and §10.3 expansion is textual, so the parentheses are load-bearing. Line 16 uses it only inside 1.0/(`P_U0_OLD * `P_C * `P_C), where explicit outer parens hide the question, and the four selector fixtures check `P_U0 in isolation. A compiler that drops the parentheses passes all five. Verified arithmetic: 1.0/`P_U0_OLD = 795774.7154594767; without the parentheses the same text is (1.0/4.0e-7)*pi = 7853981.633974483, a factor of 9.87 out.
expected: Delete lines 7-9. Add //! lrm D.2. Add the discriminating bare division: `CHECKR("P_U0_OLD keeps its parentheses under expansion", 1.0/`P_U0_OLD, 795774.7154594767, 1e-15);  Promote the two existing CHECKRs to CHECKX — 4.0e-7*M_PI = 1.2566370614359173e-6 and 1.0/(u0*c*c) = 8.854187817620389e-12 are the exact double results (pure mul/div, no FMA contraction, README documents strict IEEE in every optimize mode).

title: The fixture that claims to pin the literal standard discipline names declares all three of them itself
detail: Lines 9-18 declare `electrical`, `voltage` and `current` locally, shadowing the prelude's identical declarations, so line 22's CHECK(V(p), 0.9, 1e-12) says nothing about the implementation's disciplines.vams. `voltage` and `current` are declared and never bound, so the signal-flow half of the file's own stated claim is unasserted. (Note: the local re-declaration is legal — VerA scopes discipline uniqueness per-file deliberately, src/ir/lower.zig:760-768 — so this is an oracle defect, not a reject candidate.)

title: literal_thermal_discipline.va re-declares `thermal` before testing it
detail: Lines 8-11 declare `discipline thermal; potential Temperature; flow Power; enddiscipline` locally, duplicating the prelude's. The CHECKX(Temp(p), 350.0) on line 15 is then made against the fixture's own declaration; a compiler with no disciplines.vams passes. The binding claim is otherwise sound (if Temp were the flow, the probe reads 0.0) and 350.0 is exact.
expected: Delete lines 8-11; the prelude supplies the discipline. Add //! lrm D.1. Keep the CHECKX. Add the flow half, which the discipline also binds and which nothing checks: `CHECKX("Pwr is the thermal flow access", Pwr(p), 0.0); placed before the contribution.

title: abstol_override_branches.va is a pure preprocessor tautology and its header says so
detail: Header lines 6-7 admit it: '`abstol` is not readable from the language, so the assertion mirrors the same `ifdef'. Both CHECKs route the fixture's own macros back to the fixture's own hand-sum — CHECK(current_abstol, 2e-12, 0.0) reads `CURRENT_ABSTOL which the fixture defined nine lines earlier, and the 69.0 sum is arithmetic over sixteen macros the fixture supplied divided by sixteen literals the fixture supplied. (The sum is arithmetically correct — verified exactly 69.0 — which is the problem: it cannot fail for any Annex D reason.) The sixteen annex_d_override_* natures are never bound to a discipline or a net, so their abstol arms are never elaborated into anything observable. The override cannot reach the real natures either: preprocessor.zig:137-138 runs constants_vams then disciplines_vams before the user source, so every prelude nature has already taken its `else default.
expected: Delete the 69.0 sum CHECK outright — macro arithmetic, unfalsifiable. Delete the current_abstol CHECK for the same reason. Keep at most one observable claim: declare ONE non-shadowing nature that takes an overridden abstol, bind it as the potential of a discipline, give the module a biased port, and assert the access binding (`CHECKX("AnnexDOvr is the potential access of the overridden nature", AnnexDOvr(p), 1.25)) so the `ifdef arm is at least elaborated. Add //! lrm D.1 //! lrm 3.6.1.2. The D.1 override rule itself is NOT assertable — see D-26.

title: Flow access on a `voltage` net and potential access on a `current` net are silently accepted — the missing reject with the largest blast radius
detail: D.1 declares `discipline voltage; potential Voltage; enddiscipline` and `discipline current; flow Current; enddiscipline` — signal-flow disciplines with one nature each (§3.6.2.1, ch3-datatypes.html:603). §4.4 (ch4-expressions.html:420): 'The access function name shall match the discipline declaration for the nets, ports, or branch given in the argument expression list.' A `voltage` net has no flow nature, so `I(p)` names nothing. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION: `module m(p); inout p; voltage p; analog I(p) <+ 1.0; endmodule` compiles clean, exit 0, no diagnostic. Root cause is documented in the code: src/ir/lower.zig:1683 checkAccessMatch returns early when 'the discipline binds no nature for that half'. No fixture in the entire suite declares a net of either discipline.

title: Turn discrete_disciplines.va into the natureless-discipline reject it should always have been
detail: Today it declares `logic_disc` (a name that appears nowhere in Annex D) and `ddiscrete`, then uses neither: the body is `electrical p; analog I(p) <+ V(p);`. No CHECK, no reject — unasserted; and `module annex_d_discrete;` is portless, so the torture run reports CANNOT RUN and it never executes (confirmed in a live run). LRM 3.6.3 (ch3-datatypes.html:795, section header confirmed at line 766 = '3.6.3 Net_discipline declaration'): 'Nets declared with a natureless discipline or declared without a discipline do not have declared natures, so such nets can not be used in analog behavioral descriptions (because the access functions are not known).' That is a real prohibition and it is not being made. VERIFIED: `module m(p); inout p; \logic p ; analog V(p) <+ 0.0; endmodule` compiles clean today. NOTE the uncovered lens cited §3.5 for this sentence — wrong, it is §3.6.3; use 3.6.3.

title: literal_logic_discipline.va re-declares `\logic` and then never references it — the escaped-identifier lookup it claims to pin is untested
detail: Its header claims 'The escaped identifier is the literal standard discrete discipline name', but it declares `discipline \logic ; domain discrete; enddiscipline` itself (a verbatim duplicate of the prelude's, preprocessor.zig disciplines_vams) and then uses `electrical p`. The fixture passes identically with the declaration deleted and no standard \logic in existence. Unasserted and portless -> CANNOT RUN (confirmed live). Using the PRELUDE's escaped name puts §2.7.1 escaped-identifier termination under test as well: the trailing space in `\logic p ;` is part of the token, and a compiler that lexes `\logic` without it will not match the declared discipline.

title: A standard access function that belongs to a DIFFERENT standard discipline must not resolve — Q and Temp on an electrical net
detail: D.1 declares 16 natures but binds only 12 into disciplines. Charge (access Q, abstol 1e-14) and the thermal Temperature (access Temp) are perfectly well-declared standard access names that match no electrical net. §4.4 makes this an error, and checkAccessMatch's own doc comment names the failure mode ('every name that belongs to SOME discipline resolves on EVERY net'). No fixture calls Q(, Acc(, Imp( or Alpha( anywhere in the suite. VERIFIED: VerA DOES reject both today — Q(p) on an electrical net gives E0501 'unknown access function: `Q`' and Temp(p) gives E0501 '`Temp` is not an access function of `p`', both citing LRM 3.6.1.4. So NO xfail is needed; this is a free, immediately-green reject fixture.

title: MMF and Phi are never called anywhere in the suite; the fixture named for them asserts nothing
detail: The whole file is four lines of local `discipline magnetic` plus `module annex_d_literal_magnetic; electrical p; analog I(p) <+ V(p); endmodule`. Three stacked defects: unasserted, the discipline duplicates the prelude's, and it is never bound to a net. Portless -> CANNOT RUN (confirmed live). grep finds zero calls to MMF( or Phi( in the entire suite. The normatively interesting part — magnetic's FLOW nature is the same Flux that D.1 gives as Voltage's idt_nature, there is no separate Magnetic_Flux — is exercised by nothing. VERIFIED: `magnetic p; Phi(p) <+ MMF(p);` compiles clean against the prelude.

title: Pos, Vel and F are never called; the kinematic pair's shared-flow-nature structure is untested
detail: Same triple defect as D-15: unasserted, both disciplines duplicate the prelude's, module is portless -> CANNOT RUN, body is `electrical p; analog I(p) <+ V(p);`. Zero calls to Pos(, Vel( or F( in the suite. The pair is the interesting case: `kinematic` = potential Position (Pos) / flow Force (F), `kinematic_v` = potential Velocity (Vel) / SAME flow Force — two different potential natures sharing one flow nature, so a compiler that keys a discipline's flow access off the potential nature passes kinematic and fails kinematic_v. VERIFIED: a module with both a kinematic and a rotational_omega port using F/Tau/Pos/Omega compiles clean.

title: Theta, Omega and Tau are never called; the rotational pair repeats the kinematic shared-flow structure and is equally untested
detail: Unasserted, both disciplines duplicate the prelude's, portless -> CANNOT RUN, body is `electrical p; analog I(p) <+ V(p);`. Zero calls to Theta(, Omega( or Tau( in the suite. D.1: `rotational` = potential Angle (Theta) / flow Angular_Force (Tau); `rotational_omega` = potential Angular_Velocity (Omega) / same Angular_Force.

title: Delete magnetic_definitions.va — a dead near-duplicate of D-15 with three unused declarations attached
detail: Declares `nature Magneto_Motive_Force` and `discipline magnetic_d`, then the body is `electrical p; analog I(p) <+ V(p);` — magnetic_d is never bound to anything. No CHECK, no reject; portless -> CANNOT RUN (confirmed live). The nature name is a verbatim same-name redeclaration of the prelude's, so the only thing the declarations demonstrate is that VerA tolerates it. Once D-15 binds a real `magnetic` net and probes MMF against the implementation's own header, this file covers nothing.
expected: File removed. If a user-declared-nature claim (LRM 3.6.1) is genuinely wanted, keep it instead but rename the nature so it does not shadow the prelude (nature My_MMF, access MyMMF), bind it in magnetic_d, add a port and //! bias, and assert `CHECKX("MyMMF is the magnetic_d potential access", MyMMF(p), 3.0). Pick one; do not leave both.

title: Delete kinematic_definitions.va — 39 lines of transcription, zero assertions, never runs
detail: Declares five natures (Position, Velocity, Acceleration, Impulse, Force), every one a same-name duplicate of the prelude's, plus two disciplines bound to no net. Body is `electrical p; analog I(p) <+ V(p);`. No CHECK, no reject; portless -> CANNOT RUN (confirmed live). The idt_nature/ddt_nature chain Position<->Velocity<->Acceleration<->Impulse it transcribes is asserted nowhere — transcription is not coverage.
expected: File removed; D-16 covers the kinematic bindings against the implementation's own disciplines.vams. If the ddt/idt chain is to be pinned it needs a fixture that OBSERVES it — a numeric CHECK on a kinematic net with //! time history, not a copy of the declarations.

title: Delete rotational_definitions.va — same dead pattern as D-19
detail: Declares Angle / Angular_Velocity / Angular_Acceleration / Angular_Force (all same-name duplicates of the prelude's) and two disciplines, none bound to a net. Body is `electrical p; analog I(p) <+ V(p);`. No CHECK, no reject; portless -> CANNOT RUN (confirmed live).
expected: File removed; D-17 covers the rotational bindings against the implementation's disciplines.vams.

title: thermal_definitions.va declares thermal_d and then tests the prelude's `thermal` instead
detail: It declares `nature Temperature`, `nature Power` and `discipline thermal_d` (lines 9-22) — but line 24's port is `thermal p;`, not `thermal_d p;`. thermal_d is never used and both assertions run against the prelude's `thermal`, making the file a near-duplicate of literal_thermal_discipline.va with three dead declarations attached. Unlike its siblings it DOES have a port and DOES assert, and its numbers are correct: 400.0 exact, 400-273.15 = 126.85 verified 2.8e-14 inside the 1e-12 tolerance.
expected: Bind what it declares: change the port to `thermal_d p;` and rename the natures so they do not shadow the prelude (My_Temperature/MyTemp, My_Power/MyPwr), making this a genuine user-declaration fixture with //! lrm 3.6.1 //! lrm 3.6.2. Once D-06 removes celsius_constant.va's local define, replace the hard-coded 273.15 on line 27 with the annex macro so the second check reads `CHECK("400 K is 126.85 degC", MyTemp(p) - `P_CELSIUS0, 126.85, 1e-12). If that is not wanted, delete the file as redundant with D-09 — but then D-09 must absorb the Celsius check.

title: electrical_definitions.va declares voltage_d and current_d and asserts nothing about either
detail: Four natures and three disciplines are declared; only electrical_d is bound to a net and only its potential is probed. voltage_d (potential-only) and current_d (flow-only) are dead declarations, and the idt_nature/ddt_nature links to Charge and Flux the file transcribes are never observed. The one assertion it makes, CHECK(V(p), 0.7, 1e-12), is sound. The least-bad of the *_definitions.va family, but one assertion covering a seventh of what it declares. COVERAGE.md sD-1 additionally names this file as the evidence for the DISCIPLINES_VAMS guard, which it does not test — it carries a private ANNEX_D_ELECTRICAL_DEFINITIONS guard and its own comment admits the standard name is already taken by the prelude.

title: The DISCIPLINES_VAMS / CONSTANTS_VAMS include guards are not tested in either direction
detail: D.1 opens `ifdef DISCIPLINES_VAMS / `else / `define DISCIPLINES_VAMS 1 and closes `endif; D.2 does the same for CONSTANTS_VAMS. The idempotence rule — including the file twice must not produce a duplicate-nature or duplicate-discipline error — is tested by nothing. COVERAGE.md claims electrical_definitions.va covers the guard; it uses a private guard name and its own comment says the standard one is already taken. VERIFIED: two consecutive `include "disciplines.vams" lines compile clean today, so this is a cheap green positive fixture. The suppression direction (`define DISCIPLINES_VAMS 1 ahead of the include, making `electrical` undeclared) is NOT expressible and was dropped — the prelude sets the guard before any user text, so the `define is a no-op and no diagnostic can be provoked.

title: A nature identifier as the trailing argument of ddt/idt/idtmod is accepted by nothing in the suite
detail: §5.5.3 final sentence (ch5-analog.html, Syntax 5-4 block): 'The abstol attribute of a nature may also be accessed simply by using the nature's identifier as the appropriate argument to the ddt(), idt(), or idtmod() operators described in 4.5.' Combined with D.1's nature declarations this is the one reachable exercise of the nature-identifier form. COVERAGE.md's sD-1 row claims idt_nature/ddt_nature relationships are exercised; no fixture writes ddt or idt with a nature argument at all. src/ir/lower.zig:1833 records that VerA ignores the second argument, so the claim is acceptance plus numeric transparency, not a tolerance effect. IMPORTANT SCOPE LIMIT found by execution: `ddt(V(p), Voltage)` compiles, but `idt(V(p), Charge)` is REJECTED with E0314 'unknown identifier: `Charge`' — Charge is bound to no discipline, so VerA never registers the name. Per the LRM that rejection is wrong, but a positive fixture cannot be xfail'd, so the fixture must use only discipline-bound natures.

title: Not one fixture in the chapter carries a `//! lrm` cite
detail: Verified: all 23 .va files have zero //! lrm lines. README.md makes --coverage the only mechanical backing for a claim that a clause is covered, so with no cites this chapter contributes nothing to that set, and a failing fixture here prints no rule. Every fixture pins exactly one of three clauses, so this is mechanical. It becomes a hard requirement the moment D-11/D-12/D-13/D-14 land, since //! lrm is required on every reject fixture.
expected: //! lrm D.1 on the surviving D.1 fixtures (abstol_override_branches, discrete_disciplines, electrical_definitions, literal_electrical_disciplines, literal_kinematic_disciplines, literal_logic_discipline, literal_magnetic_discipline, literal_rotational_disciplines, literal_thermal_discipline, thermal_definitions and the new rejects); //! lrm D.2 on celsius_constant, mathematical_constants, vacuum_constants and the five physical_constants_*; //! lrm D.3 on both driver_flags_*. Plus //! lrm 3.6.3 on D-12/D-13, //! lrm 4.4 on D-11/D-14. Fold into each item above rather than doing a separate sweep, and verify with `zig build torture -- --coverage`.

title: COVERAGE.md claims coverage the fixtures do not provide, and must record the four things that are genuinely untestable
detail: Row sD-1 says default tolerances and idt_nature/ddt_nature relationships 'are exercised by' the *_definitions.va files and that abstol_override_branches.va 'defines and selects all 16 published _ABSTOL override arms'. Eight of the fixtures it names assert nothing and are CANNOT RUN (confirmed in a live run: 15/23 behave as stated, 8 CANNOT RUN). Row sD-2 admits the shape of the problem — 'these fixtures validate preprocessing and lowering of the literal names and values' — but what they actually validate is the fixtures' own `define lines. This row also carries the four claims I DROPPED as fixture work because no conforming fixture can express them, and they must be written down here instead of silently disappearing: (1) the 16 published abstols are unreadable — §5.5.3's nature_attribute_reference is normative and makes p.potential.abstol a constant expression, but VerA does not parse it (verified: E0207 'unexpected token: found .'; src/frontend/parser.zig:1457 documents the omission), and a positive fixture cannot be xfail'd; (2) the D.1 _ABSTOL override rule is therefore unobservable, even though the plumbing works (`undef DISCIPLINES_VAMS + re-include compiles clean, verified) — the effect lands only in codegen's per-node abstol, lower.zig:104; (3) the sixteen units strings cannot be asserted for the same reason, so 'units ... are exercised by electrical_definitions.va' is false; (4) driver_access.vams is not supplied — `include "driver_access.vams" is E0126 (verified), and preprocessor.zig:110 carries the ponytail note explaining the omission, so D.3 is transcribed rather than tested until builtin_includes gains a third entry.
expected: Restate sD-1 as 'the standard discipline names and their potential/flow access bindings are probed on live nets of the implementation-supplied disciplines'. State plainly under sD-1 that the <NATURE>_ABSTOL override arms and the published abstol/units values are NOT covered, with the §5.5.3-vs-parser reason. Under sD-2, drop the physical_constants_select.vh sentence and the trailing note at lines 84-85, and state that the selector arms are now reached via `undef CONSTANTS_VAMS + re-include. Under sD-3, state that driver_access.vams is not supplied by the implementation. Refresh the literal fixture inventory after the three deletions in D-18/19/20 and the D-04 .vh removal. Also note the E0314-on-unbound-nature gap from D-24.
